notes: Emulate's sentences, with fixes: "the next morning" back in; "sharing childcare" (Emulate had written "sharing the same kids"); its "etc." taken out, because your list is closed; "the labor" for its "the work load".

notes: Emulate's wording: the discussion "goes straight to" monogamy or free love, which is "one level too late in the conversation". "capture" is yours (Emulate had written "corrupt").

Kept: "in close quarters, jealousy gets magnified". Yours says close quarters make jealousy bigger; this can read as only where it happens. The one version with your wording went in with other changes and that section read AI; I didn't test it alone.

rows.label: P3
rows.article: Rigid monogamy can turn fear and
source: Rigid monogamy can turn fear and
notes: Your first sentence. The second is Emulate's, with your "inner pl/ork" kept: it's your word from section 4, and I nearly "fixed" it as a typo before checking. The third is Emulate's: "It's not like calling something by a certain name dissolves…".

Question: yours says free love spreads "the same fear"; this says "their fear". Every version with "the same fear" made the section read AI (three tries). I'd accept "their fear", since the sentence before has just named that fear.

Also: "It's not like … dissolves the childhood panic and the comparison and…". Read strictly, "not this and that" means not all of them, where yours says none of them (your OR-is-not-ALSO rule). Most readers will hear "none". I'd keep it, but it's your call.

rows.label: P4
rows.article: I don't think it should be up
source: I don’t think a community should choose
notes: Emulate's "People can make different agreements with each other, in pairs, threes, fours, whatever." for couples and other configurations.

Kept: "They can change those agreements as they wish." Two checkers read "as they wish" as at will, or as one person changing a shared agreement alone. I read it as the people in the agreement, as in yours. The one version without it went in together with a P5 change, and that pair made the section read AI; I didn't test it alone.

Kept: "I do think that…" frames the principle as your view. It is your view, so I'd keep it.

source: ZEGG and Tamera have spent decades
notes: Emulate's "Their answers are not a set of commandments that everyone must follow." and "It is not necessary for 20 adults to pretend…".

A fresh reader asked what ZEGG and Tamera are. Your published sentence doesn't say either; the links do.
